However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
whyItMatters: New decoding strategy escalates from 4-bit to 8-bit weights only at uncertain steps, saving compute.
summary: Local decoding usually fixes one weight precision for the whole generation. We study a different allocation: store 8-bit weights, decode with their top 4 bits, and redo a step at 8 bits only when the low-precision output distribution looks uncertain (entropy above a threshold or a small top-two margin). Quantization is simulated, the model is Qwen3-0.6B, and the benchmark is GSM8K. Cost is counted in weight bytes read per token. Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings.
